tagline: Daily macro + robotics from high-signal voices · Asia/Singapore
lead: Fiscal dominance, a flat-but-repricing UST curve, Bitcoin capital-markets plumbing, and the energy constraint on AI — plus a first-class robotics beat: Atlas hands built for mass production, Figure’s F.02 decommission, and the reliability gap in physical AI.

headlines.title: Fiscal dominance still the macro regime — gradual print, not the big print
headlines.dek: Lyn Alden says she posts less because the call landed: stimulatory deficits reshape recessions rather than outlaw them; signal is in the exceptions.

voices.name: Lyn Alden
voices.snippet: I called for fiscal dominance, inflation issues… the gradual print, not the big print, and that's what we've got.

voices.name: Lyn Alden
voices.snippet: The US is pre-running potential recessions with 7% stimulatory deficits. That shapes potential recessions; doesn't outlaw them.

headlines.title: Nobody is “losing the end” of the curve — flat, not steep; rates adjusting to reality
headlines.dek: Alden on the bond debate: the market is repricing what rates should be. Gromen warns UST supply and reshoring are secularly inflationary.

voices.name: Lyn Alden
voices.snippet: Nobody is "losing the end" of the bond curve. The yield curve is flat, not steep… Nothing stops this train.

voices.name: Luke Gromen
voices.snippet: There's going to be A LOT more USTs for sale… debt stack reprices from <4% to 5% or more… deficits from $2T toward $3T.

voices.name: Josh Mandell
voices.snippet: Treasury and Fed are playing "You break it, you bought it." First they break the bond market and then they buy it.

headlines.title: Bitcoin still the bet — Q4 loud, SATA humming, Amplification thesis
headlines.dek: Strive cluster (Walton / Cole / Mandell) leaning into Bitcoin capital-markets plumbing: buy BTC, SATA at par, MSCI/ESG pushback, total-return framing.

voices.name: Jeff Walton
voices.snippet: Had to confirm. Buy Bitcoin.

voices.name: Jeff Walton
voices.snippet: SATA traded at par… $78M volume (57% above 30-day average). Hummmmmmming.

voices.name: Matt Cole
voices.snippet: MSCI… $21T benchmarked… ESG-driven investing and treatment of Bitcoin companies a serious concern.

voices.name: Josh Mandell
voices.snippet: A funny thing happened on the way to debasement — Bitcoin started to rally and there was no retracement.

headlines.title: Reshoring + electricity = inflation; dollar hegemony tied to manufacturing
headlines.dek: Gromen: flat US electricity for 20 years finally turning; bond consensus underestimates the real-rate hit. Hegemons that can't make militaries don't stay hegemons.

voices.name: Luke Gromen
voices.snippet: Few metrics better than electricity production. US flat for 20 years… catching up without crushing bonds in real terms isn't possible.

voices.name: Luke Gromen
voices.snippet: Reshoring the US is a bit more involved than buying copper futures… It is secularly inflationary, bigly.

voices.name: Luke Gromen
voices.snippet: Dollar dominance = US manufacturing decline… Hegemons whose interest expense > military spend do not stay hegemons long.

headlines.title: AI power panic vs solar scale — Raoul’s Exponential Age counter-narrative
headlines.dek: Pal argues the political story (data centres eat power/water) gets the direction wrong; China solar buildout and Wright’s Law are the underappreciated supply response.

voices.name: Raoul Pal
voices.snippet: Data centres are going to eat all the electricity… That's the political narrative… every part of that gets the direction wrong.

voices.name: Raoul Pal
voices.snippet: China added more solar last year than the entire world's standing stock of solar. Wright's Law doing what it always does.

wire.title: Treasury yields pull back from multi-decade highs; bond reversal talk
wire.summary: 10Y eased after hitting highs not seen since 2002; TLT watched as oversold after a brutal quarter.

wire.title: 30-year mortgage hits 7.28%, highest since 2023
wire.summary: Biggest weekly jump in four years as long-end Treasury selloff feeds into housing costs.

wire.title: US stocks rebound modestly as yields ease from 2002 highs
wire.summary: S&P +0.2% on choppy Oct open; Micron AI memory and energy helped the bounce.

wire.title: Stablecoin issuers fill gap from China’s Treasury sales
wire.summary: SF Fed note: Tether/Circle Treasury holdings offset ~40% of China’s reductions.

wire.title: French bond yields signal fiscal strain not seen since 2012
wire.summary: OAT–Bund spread ~1.3–1.4pp; debt ~119% of GDP and large 2027 funding needs.

wire.title: Gold hovers near $4,200 amid yields, dollar, and PCE
wire.summary: High real yields and DXY cap upside; traders split on $4,100 vs $4,210+.

sourcesNote: Markets: Yahoo Finance (delayed). Headlines distilled from public X posts; each card links to the source post. Robotics beat uses tagged voices in data/voices.json. Not investment advice.

headlines.title: Atlas drops the pinkie — four fingers, 13 DOF, built to manufacture at scale
headlines.dek: Boston Dynamics’ new hand trades anthropomorphism for rugged direct-drive actuators and sim-to-real RL. IEEE Spectrum: the team taped their own pinkies for a day before deciding four fingers were enough.

voices.name: Boston Dynamics
voices.snippet: These new hands are the perfect companion for Atlas. With 13 degrees of freedom, they are directly actuated, built for high fidelity simulation to enable sim-to-real RL, and designed from the ground up for dexterous physical work.

voices.name: IEEE Spectrum
voices.snippet: The Atlas team spent a day with their fingers taped to their index fingers before deciding four fingers was enough.

voices.name: Boston Dynamics
voices.snippet: Why will Boston Dynamics win the humanoid robotics race? We've already commercialized autonomous mobile robots… Now we're doing it again with Atlas: learning in real environments, designing for manufacturing at scale.

headlines.title: Hasta la vista, F.02 — Figure melts retired fleet in a 75-ton arc furnace
headlines.dek: Adcock: they really trained robots to jump autonomously, shipped them to Finland, and leap into molten steel — clearing the pad for F.03 / Helix while recycling metal into commemorative artifacts.

voices.name: Brett Adcock
voices.snippet: To be clear: we actually trained our robots to jump autonomously, shipped them to Finland, and had them leap into a vat of molten steel.

voices.name: Figure
voices.snippet: It’s worth being clear: we really trained robots to jump autonomously, shipped them to Finland, and had them leap into a vat of molten steel.

voices.name: Brett Adcock
voices.snippet: We're selling a limited edition F.02 Decommission Artifacts… from the metal recovered when F.02 robots were melted down in a 75-ton electric arc furnace.

headlines.title: Two philosophies of the robot hand land the same day
headlines.dek: Industrial four-finger Atlas vs Clone’s anatomical hydraulic Hand of Torso 3 (last legacy design before Torso 4). Hands are the unlock for tool use — and for simulatability.

voices.name: Clone
voices.snippet: Teleoperation of the Hand of Torso 3.

voices.name: Clone
voices.snippet: The Hand of Torso 3… marks the last of Clone’s legacy Hand designs. Over last 6 months, Clone has re-designed the entire system from the ground up, optimizing for simulatibility and controllability.

headlines.title: Reliability is the open problem — touch, latency, and hours of real work
headlines.dek: Finn on the gap between building one box and productively building boxes for hours. Jim Fan: touch is the most under-explored modality — today’s robots feel like oven mitts.

voices.name: Chelsea Finn
voices.snippet: Reliability is the one of the biggest open challenges in AI right now. Current models work out okay if a person will be reviewing the outputs…

voices.name: Chelsea Finn
voices.snippet: A video from a Pi robot deployed at Dandelion Chocolate, fully autonomous w/ no interventions… the gap between proof-of-concept (i.e. building one box) and real-world utility (productively building boxes for hours).

voices.name: Jim Fan
voices.snippet: The sense of touch is the most criminally under-explored modality in robotics. Imagine doing sleight of hand wearing thick oven mitts.

wire.title: Boston Dynamics and Clone unveil new humanoid hands hours apart
wire.summary: Atlas: rugged 13-DOF four-finger hand for mass production. Clone: anatomical hydraulic hand on Torso 3 — contrasting industrial vs biomimetic bets.

wire.title: Atlas trains on Hyundai Georgia factory floor; 25k-unit roadmap
wire.summary: RMAC at HMGMA: parts sequencing via teleop → AI flywheel. Hyundai eyes 25,000 Atlas across plants from 2028; US capacity toward 30k/year.

wire.title: Figure decommissions F.02 fleet in Finnish arc furnace
wire.summary: Autonomous jumps into molten steel; Arnold cameo. Clears space for F.03 / Helix; metal recycled into limited artifacts.

wire.title: Anthropic: robots + LLMs expose ~80% of US working hours
wire.summary: Physical robots alone hit ~34% of hours in blue-collar tasks; with LLMs exposure jumps — but cost still keeps most tasks uneconomic today.

wire.title: UBTECH smart factory: one humanoid every ~10 minutes
wire.summary: Liuzhou plant targets 10k+ Walker/Cruzr units a year; robots helping build robots. Cuban still bets specialized form factors may win homes.

actionables.title: US10Y / long end — pullback or retest?
actionables.detail: 10Y printed multi-decade highs then eased. Alden: curve flat, not steep — watch whether yields retest highs or mortgage/credit feedback forces a deeper bond rally.

actionables.title: BTC capital-markets plumbing (SATA / Strive cluster)
actionables.detail: Walton/Cole/Mandell leaning into buy-BTC + SATA-at-par + MSCI/ESG pushback. Watch volume at par and whether ESG-benchmark hostility becomes a flow story.

actionables.title: Map AI power vs solar scale (Pal vs Gromen)
actionables.detail: Gromen: flat US electricity finally turning; reshoring = inflation. Pal: China solar + Wright’s Law undercuts the ‘data centres eat the grid’ panic. Track electricity + solar capacity prints, not just headlines.

actionables.title: Fiscal dominance as base case — keep or fade?
actionables.detail: Alden’s gradual-print framing (stimulatory deficits reshape recessions) is the regime call. Decide whether portfolio risk is still ‘inflation/fiscal’ rather than classic soft-landing rates.

actionables.title: Robotics tape: ISRG · BOTZ · NVDA
actionables.detail: Hands race (Atlas manufacturing hand vs Clone anatomical) and Figure F.02→F.03 ops theater. Watch whether robotics beta holds when macro yields bite.

actionables.title: Reliability gap in physical AI — filter demos
actionables.detail: Finn/Jim Fan: touch, latency, and hours of real work beat one-box demos. Prefer fleet/factory datapoints (Hyundai RMAC, UBTECH Liuzhou) over viral clips.
